_doc: What each of the 18 Mistheim Peoples (the Wildkin added 2026-10-11, #1606; the Riksfolk and the Strandfolk, #1623) values, shames, does and believes about the others (#1590). Written for the knowledge model (#1577 slice C) and for claims, rumours and lies (#1580); read through src/artificer/culture-lore.ts. Every claim names its source (file § heading › label); invented: true marks what canon doesn't say, built on that source. A claim with truth rumour or false says what is actually so. docs/culture-lore.md explains it.

voice.text: Plain and short. They name the thing, say what it's for, and stop. Praise is a nod at good work.

values.text: We ask what you have made, not whose child you are.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

values.text: Skill you can see and hold is worth more than clever talk.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

values.text: Patience: eight hundred years of craft, each smith adding to what the last one learned.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What they make

taboos.text: Taking someone's tools without asking. It's the worst thing you can do in the Dyprike.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Bergfolk › Objects

taboos.text: Sitting in a hold seat you only inherited and never earned.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

taboos.text: Talking about using Rasa. A runesmith who does keeps it to themself.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Bergfolk

greeting.text: You show your hands and say what you make. Your work is your name.
greeting.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

trade.text: Mana-granite is sold in standard sizes, and the runes on every block say who cut it.

mourning.text: A master runesmith is buried with their own tools. No one else may use them.

debt.text: We remember a debt as long as we remember a grudge, and that is a long time.
debt.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Dwarves

Lövfolk.text: The elves want the eastern hardwood left standing. We need it for charcoal. Neither side has moved in centuries.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

Lövfolk.text: Our mana-granite does the forest no harm.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

actually.text: Bergfolk mana-granite channels are disrupting the Myst at the forest's western edge. Nobody has admitted it officially.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

Lövfolk.text: Elf healing is feeling, not real magic.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § Who uses it and how › The Bergfolk

actually.text: Lövfolk Rasa is quiet and very effective: their healers have wanted patients to heal for centuries.
actually.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Lövfolk

Markfolk.text: We trade them ore for food. The quarrel over the southern foothills never quite ends.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

Viddfolk.text: We trust a Viddfolk herald with a hold's contracts. They never take sides.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

Viddfolk.text: A Viddfolk herald still runs a main route in three days.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › The Dry's effect

actually.text: The ley-lines are thinning. Heralds now take four or five days, and the Viddfolk keep it to themselves.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › The Dry's effect

Steinfolk.text: The nearest thing we have to true friends. They build; we give them what to build with.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

Pandor.text: Pandor scholars make nothing you can hold in your hands.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

actually.text: The Pandor make the continent's best maps, its records, and the mist-ferment poured at every serious negotiation.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What they make

Deepwalkers.text: Deepwalker salt keeps a hold's meat through the winter. We buy it by the barrel.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › What they make

Merfolk.text: Merfolk pressure-crystal makes the finest enchanting. They sell it slowly, and only when they choose.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What they make

Goblins.text: There are no goblins in our holds.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

actually.text: Goblin salvage bands live in the empty upper levels of three old holds. They're so useful nobody in charge has looked.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

Fae.text: A fae bargain binds tighter than any rune. We don't make them.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Giants.text: Don't wake a sleeping giant, and don't take from its land without asking.

Dragons.text: Iskuldr keeps our tribute tools and never uses them. That means he approves.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

actually.text: Iskuldr keeps every tool and has used none. The Bergfolk read that as approval; nobody knows what he thinks.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: Vitstad's liches have been levelling their craft for two hundred years. We'd rather not talk about it.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Relations

Constructs.text: A construct is a made thing, not a person.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

actually.text: Under the Compact of Knowing constructs are persons. The old ones have Classes; the newer Bergfolk-made ones don't, yet.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: Ask a Remnant a question and you get a true answer you can't use. We'd rather ask a stone.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: The beastkin at the pass-towns trade fair. Why we're coming out of the mountains is hold business.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § West — The Mountains › Dvergr

Riksfolk.text: The Realm has bought a great deal of our iron lately. We have started asking what it's for.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › started asking what it's for

Strandfolk.text: Shipwrights. They buy our nails by the barrel and complain by the barrel.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Scarce: farmland, metal

sayings.text: Don't ask whose child. Ask what they made.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

sayings.text: Never touch another smith's tools.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § Bergfolk › Objects

sayings.text: A crude tool is a promise you'll fix it later.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › hf-orrin

voice.text: Unhurried and layered. What they mean sits under what they say, and nothing is said in a rush.

values.text: Memory that lasts lifetimes: the oldest trees keep what happened, and we keep the trees.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What they make

values.text: Healing that is meant. Our healers have wanted patients well for two hundred years and know the feeling exactly.
values.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Lövfolk

values.text: Wood is taken from the forest sparingly, and with ceremony.
values.source: WORLD.md § Lövfolk › Objects

taboos.text: Felling a living tree to build with. We shape trees over generations; we don't cut them.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Lövfolk › Architecture

taboos.text: Hurrying an elder to change their mind. It's rude, and it takes an earthquake anyway.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What shapes them

greeting.text: A slow nod and a long look. Answering too fast says you weren't listening.

trade.text: Grenmark bows and herbal compounds are sold. Reading the memory-trees is traded only between nations.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What they make

mourning.text: Mourners say the dead one's name beneath an old tree, so the tree will keep it.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What they make

debt.text: A gift of living-wood jewellery is a bond. It keeps growing as long as the bond is kept.

Bergfolk.text: They want our hardwood for charcoal. They will not have it.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

Bergfolk.text: Their mana-granite is thinning the Myst at our western edge. No one has said so out loud.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

Markfolk.text: Farming is humble work. It takes no great skill.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What they make

actually.text: Markfolk [Watermasters] reach levels other nations find embarrassing. A Level 35 Watermaster outranks many a [Knight].
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What they make

Viddfolk.text: Viddfolk heralds carry our councils' letters, and we trust them to forget nothing.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

Steinfolk.text: A Steinfolk bridge stands at our forest's edge where the old one rotted. They built it when nobody else would.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Where they live

Pandor.text: The friendship that works: they need our trees' memories, and we need their neutral ground for our quarrels.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

Deepwalkers.text: Fellow keepers of memory, under the Compact of Knowing.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Compact of Knowing

Merfolk.text: The Merfolk's wares keep their full strength while our enchantments weaken. They say nothing about it.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › The Dry's effect

Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The two traditions together › Goblins

actually.text: Goblins have Classes and Skills like anyone. They are people; the world doesn't agree, and the world is wrong.
actually.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Goblins

Fae.text: The fae were under our groves before the trees were saplings. Neither of us can make the other leave.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

Giants.text: Giants live too slowly even for us. We can wait a long time; they wait longer.

Dragons.text: Grimmvald's patronage takes our young ones and gives back strangers.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

actually.text: Several young Lövfolk have taken Grimmvald's patronage. They come back changed and say little; what it means is unclear.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: The Pale City keeps its records nearly as long as our trees do. We share them under the Compact.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Compact of Knowing

Constructs.text: A construct cannot change. It stays as it was made.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

actually.text: Older constructs have developed Classes; several became [Scholars] or [Keepers].
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: The Remnants are what the dead gods left. We don't say the gods' names, and we don't ask.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The weight of the past

Wildkin.text: The beastkin's Great Clans won't add new council seats. We know that problem well.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › THE CLAN QUESTION

Riksfolk.text: The Realm has changed its whole shape several times since I was young. Humans call that history.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › a single Lövfolk

Strandfolk.text: Humans live too briefly to learn the sea. The Strandfolk only guess.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › short lives

actually.text: Strandfolk build most of the hulls on Mistheim's coasts, and Strandfolk crews sail them.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Strandfolk crews sail them

sayings.text: A healing word works better when it is true.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › cv-ottilia

sayings.text: Listen to the wound before you touch it.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › hf-isa

sayings.text: The tree remembers.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What they make

voice.text: Dry and understated. They know exactly how much everyone needs them, and joke about it only among themselves.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What shapes them

values.text: Feeding people. Half the continent eats our grain, whether it thanks us or not.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What they make

values.text: Patience with water: a [Watermaster] feels where the river wants to go.
values.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Markfolk

values.text: Keeping records for generations. A good farmer knows their land's yields six generations back.
values.source: WORLD.md § Markfolk › Objects

taboos.text: Wasting water. On the plains it's the worst kind of carelessness.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What they make

taboos.text: Boasting. Let the harvest speak; a Markfolk who brags gets laughed at, dryly.
taboos.source: AXES.md § Notes on individual scores › Markfolk

greeting.text: A tip of the broad hat, and a question about the weather that's really about the crops.

trade.text: Goods go to market in clay urns with the owner's mark pressed into the clay.

mourning.text: The dead one's name goes into the seed book, beside the last harvest they brought in.

debt.text: Debts are settled in the meeting hall, in front of the river charts, so everyone knows it's done.

Bergfolk.text: They eat our grain and sell us metal at a markup. We smile, and count.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What shapes them

Bergfolk.text: Ore for food, and a foothills quarrel that flares and cools every twenty years or so.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › Relations

Lövfolk.text: The elves think they're better than everyone.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Elves

actually.text: Lövfolk opinions set hard after three hundred years; their councils have held the same seats for four centuries. Their young often leave.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What shapes them

Viddfolk.text: Sixty years of talks over grazing on the eastern steppe. No war, and nobody expects an end.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › Relations

Viddfolk.text: The eastern steppe is empty land going to waste.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › Relations

actually.text: It's Viddfolk route-claim and grazing, recognised by every nation under the Vidde Accords.
actually.source: WORLD.md § Resource geography

Viddfolk.text: Where a charter fence crosses a route, the gate stands open on route days. Shut it and the council and the Viddfolk both fine you.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The eastern charters › Route gates

Steinfolk.text: They built the river works and we run them. Both of us know who needs whom.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › Relations

Pandor.text: The kloster's brew is poured at every serious meeting. Nobody calls it leverage. It is.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What they make

Deepwalkers.text: Harbour neighbours: our grain goes down the river and their salt comes up it.

Merfolk.text: The Merfolk never answer because they look down on us.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

actually.text: Merfolk answer patience, not urgency. They plan across decades; a question asked this week may be answered in years.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

Goblins.text: No goblins live in the Merkförbund. It's against the law.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What shapes them

actually.text: It is the law, but farms on the eastern edge quietly hire goblin [Salvagers], and nobody asks.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What shapes them

Fae.text: A fae deal is a trick. Never make one at the field's edge.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

actually.text: Fae deals are always technically fair. The trouble is what "fair" means to someone a thousand years old.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Giants.text: Aldriksson's valley drains in ways no surveyor can explain. Our Watermasters would love to ask him how.

Dragons.text: Dragons are wicked, and hoard gold to spite us.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Dragons

actually.text: Dragons aren't evil. Their goals just don't fit our ideas of right and wrong.
actually.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Dragons

Everstill.text: The Pale City's dead are the corruption's work.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

actually.text: The Everstill died and didn't stay dead without any help from the corruption: their Classes carried on.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Constructs.text: Constructs guard the road junctions and ruins that nobody else wants to.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: One sits at the Threefold Crossroads. Ask it a question and you'll get a true answer, and probably no help.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: Beastkin are wild things. They couldn't keep a field.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › An old, stable civilization

actually.text: The Wildkin are an old, stable kingdom of forests, meadows and market squares.
actually.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › An old, stable civilization

Riksfolk.text: Neighbours across the fens. They buy our grain in bad years and hate needing to. We count, and smile.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › Relations

Riksfolk.text: Humans can't farm wet ground. Leave them the hills.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Where they live

actually.text: Riksfolk [Dikemasters] drained the West March, and drained fen is the best soil in the lowlands.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › How the March grew

Strandfolk.text: Our grain goes to half the continent in Strandfolk hulls. They carry it, we grow it, both keep the accounts.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › Relations

sayings.text: Everyone eats our grain. Nobody says so.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What shapes them

sayings.text: A building is never finished. It just hasn't had its next room yet.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § Markfolk › Architecture

sayings.text: Water listens, if you've been patient with it long enough.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › sm-gunnar

voice.text: They speak in remembered phrases. A fact comes with the verse it's kept in, word for word.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

values.text: Memory is the highest skill. Forgetting is a failing, not an accident.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

values.text: Neutrality: we will carry a message to an enemy, and take no payment to delay it.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › Relations

values.text: Anything worth having can be carried, remembered or outrun.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

taboos.text: Taking a side, or a bribe to slow a message. We don't take sides; we take the road.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

taboos.text: Lending your ley-line instrument. A herald's is never lent.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Viddfolk › Objects

greeting.text: We read each other's woven colours first: route, clan and seniority. Then we speak.

trade.text: Prices live in the route-songs. A singer remembers both.

mourning.text: The dead one's verses are sung once more round the Speaking-Ground fire, then taught to someone young.

debt.text: The road keeps its debts: help a herald, and the next fire on the route is yours.

Bergfolk.text: We carry the holds' contracts sealed, and witness the seal broken at the other end.

Lövfolk.text: Elf councils still write as if the world were four hundred years younger. We carry the letters anyway.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What shapes them

Markfolk.text: Sixty years of talks over the eastern steppe. The Merkförbund wants to plough our route-claims.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › Relations

Markfolk.text: Merkförbund law calls our routes open land, because they have no fence. The Accords they signed say a route is ours wherever it runs.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The eastern charters › The charters

Steinfolk.text: Steinfolk bridges carry our routes over the rivers. Every one of them is in a song.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What they make

Pandor.text: The Pandor write down what we remember. Between us, nothing is lost twice.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What they make

Deepwalkers.text: Deepwalker [Keepers] remember word for word too. We respect anyone who doesn't forget.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Where they live

Merfolk.text: The Djupvolk use no roads, so they don't need us. That makes them hard to know.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places

Goblins.text: Goblins bring news out of the ruins, and we carry it to those who can use it, for a share. Nobody admits it.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › Relations

Fae.text: We carry a fae message like any other: sealed, and unread.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › Relations

Giants.text: Our oldest songs have a verse for each of the Seven. None of the verses is finished.

Dragons.text: Rödrök holds the open steppe. Our routes bend round his ground, and the song says why.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: The Everstill forget nothing either. They just never go anywhere.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City

Everstill.text: Nothing can touch the Everstill. They'll be here forever.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City

actually.text: Some of the Everstill whose lives are tied to one Myst-anchored place have found the anchor weakening. Their state may not be permanent.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › The Dry's effect

Constructs.text: A construct at a road junction never leaves its post. We like that in a neighbour.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: The Remnant who carries the Pandor's messages is never late. We respect that.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: The beastkin kingdom is small and walled by mountain and sea. Our songs give it a short verse.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › never been large

Riksfolk.text: We carry the Marshal's letters like anyone's. Every word is remembered, and she knows it.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Relations

Strandfolk.text: Harbour letters come inland with our heralds. The Strandfolk respect anyone who travels for a living.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › respect anyone who travels for a living

sayings.text: We don't take sides. We take the road.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

sayings.text: Snow tells you everything. Mud lies.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › sm-yrsa

sayings.text: Carry it, remember it, or outrun it.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

voice.text: Quiet and exact. They don't complain; they note what would stop it breaking a fifth time.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

values.text: What you leave standing is who you were.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

values.text: Coming when called: when something breaks we come, and we stay to keep it working.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What they make

values.text: No more stone than the work needs, and every stone exactly where it belongs.
values.source: WORLD.md § Steinfolk › Architecture

taboos.text: Building for show. The outside stays plain; the craft belongs inside.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Steinfolk › Architecture

taboos.text: The labyrinth stories. Most of us find them deeply rude.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Minotaurs

greeting.text: We read each other's horns: every finished project adds a mark, and an elder's are covered.

trade.text: Every big job starts with a foundation stone naming the date, the builder and who asked for it.

mourning.text: We add one stone to whatever the dead one built. If nothing is left, we cut a memorial stone and set it somewhere that matters.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

debt.text: We don't hold grudges. We remember, as data.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Relations

Bergfolk.text: Allies in the Building Alliance. We build, they supply, and we argue about method, slowly.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Relations

Lövfolk.text: We built the bridge at their forest's edge when the old one rotted. Nobody there learned to mend it.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What they make

Markfolk.text: The best partnership in Mistheim: we built the river works, and they run them.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Relations

Viddfolk.text: The Viddfolk carry word when a flood wall fails. They're why we arrive in time.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

Pandor.text: Pandor maps are the most accurate there are. We check them anyway.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What they make

Deepwalkers.text: We built the southern sea-wall when the harbour silted up. The Deepwalkers moved their stilts and came back.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Where they live

Merfolk.text: We have never built anything for the Merfolk. They have never asked.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › Resources

Goblins.text: A goblin [Mender] keeps things working that nobody else will touch. We respect that.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

Fae.text: Fae rooms don't measure true. A wall should be as long inside as out.

Giants.text: Bergamora's eastern face was built, not grown.

actually.text: The formations on Bergamora's eastern face look deliberate. Nobody knows whether they are.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

Dragons.text: No fighting on dragon ground. That's the Old Accords, and it's good sense.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Old Accords

Everstill.text: Nobody living understands how the Pale City was built. We have tried.

Constructs.text: A well-made construct is like a good arch: it keeps working long after its maker is gone.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: Remnants cause no trouble and need no upkeep. We have no other opinion.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: The beastkin have never called us. Their mountains and their sea do the work of a wall.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › have always been its walls

Riksfolk.text: Humans build in timber and earth. A Riksfolk ditch is good work, though. We'd know.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › How the March grew

Strandfolk.text: A harbour wall should be stone. The Strandfolk agree, and can't afford it.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Scarce: farmland, metal, stone

sayings.text: What you leave standing is who you were.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

sayings.text: Not a grievance. Data.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Relations

sayings.text: Build it so there's no fifth time.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

voice.text: Precise and careful, with a source for everything: "the book says".
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What shapes them

values.text: Writing everything down: weather, trade, decisions, and what witnesses saw.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What they make

values.text: Sharing what we know: under the Compact of Knowing we tell anyone who asks.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › Where they live

values.text: Keeping secrets well, in sealed records and time-locked archives.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What shapes them

taboos.text: Losing a record. A burned archive or an untaught scholar is a harm as bad as violence.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What shapes them

taboos.text: A quick answer with no source. Better slow and right.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What shapes them

greeting.text: A bow, then your name and where you've come from, so it can be written down.
greeting.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What they make

trade.text: Every sale goes in the book, and nobody argues with the book.

mourning.text: A scholar's last notes are copied out in full and read aloud, so nothing dies with them.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What shapes them

debt.text: A debt is written in two books, yours and the kloster's, and crossed out in both when it's paid.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What they make

Bergfolk.text: The finest smiths alive, and wary of anything they can't hold. We try not to take it personally.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What shapes them

Lövfolk.text: Our working friendship: we read their memory-trees, and they borrow our neutral ground.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

Lövfolk.text: Young Lövfolk [Keepers] have begun writing to us, quietly, about the trees going silent.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › The Dry's effect

Markfolk.text: Their seed books go back six generations. We admire that more than they know.

Viddfolk.text: They remember and we write. Their songs and our books disagree less often than you'd think.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What shapes them

Steinfolk.text: Every Steinfolk foundation stone is a record. We copy them.
The stronghold at the centre of the continent must guard an old ruin.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Where they live

actually.text: The Steinfolk have never said why they built at the centre, and nobody has pressed them.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Where they live

Deepwalkers.text: Our strongest allies. Their [Keepers] and our [Archivists] share the Compact's legal framework.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Relations

Merfolk.text: We asked the Djupvolk for an exchange of knowledge thirty years ago. They haven't replied yet.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

Goblins.text: They sell us what their [Delvers] find. We write it down, and must tell anyone who asks. They've never forgiven us.

Fae.text: We have written down fae magic many times. The accounts are accurate, and useless.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Fae

Giants.text: Aldriksson agreed to talk with us about the old weather. He set the meeting for next spring, fourteen months away.
Giants.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven › The Dry's effect

Dragons.text: We have formally asked Saltmara to let us study her sunken ruins. She hasn't answered.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: Vitstad is our partner in the Compact of Knowing, and one of the largest libraries in Mistheim.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Relations

Constructs.text: By our classification constructs are persons. The Bergfolk disagree.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: A Pandor scholar named them, needing something to write in the margin. One has carried our messages for two hundred years.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: Our records on the beastkin are thin. They never had a reason to look outward.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › Isolationist by geography

Riksfolk.text: The Realm has been an empire, kingdoms and a republic. Our records hold every one, and how each ended.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › It is a long list

Strandfolk.text: Strandfolk captains bring the newest charts home; the keepers remember them; our archive keeps both.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › the charts and the memory

sayings.text: Nobody argues with the book.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › hf-tobin

sayings.text: Ask, and we must tell. Very few ask.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › sm-anselm

sayings.text: A lost record is a harm, not a mistake.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Pandor — panda scholars of the highland mist › What shapes them

voice.text: Exact and quoting: they repeat what was said, word for word, and who said it.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Where they live

values.text: Memory, word for word. A [Keeper] remembers a treaty exactly as it was first spoken.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Where they live

values.text: A promise felt, not just recited: a [Keeper] feels a contract's weight as it was felt at signing.
values.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Deepwalkers

values.text: Being flexible: we aren't nomads, but we'll move the whole town if the sea asks.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Where they live

taboos.text: Misremembering. A [Keeper] who begins to forget suffers one of the worst things that can happen.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › What shapes them

taboos.text: Building something that can't be moved. The sea always gets a say.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Deepwalkers › Architecture

greeting.text: A [Keeper] shows the braid on their left wrist, and another [Keeper] reads their clan and memory-line in it.

trade.text: A contract witnessed by a Deepwalker [Keeper] binds more than signed paper ever could.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › What they make

mourning.text: A [Keeper]'s seal ring is never passed on. It is buried with them.

debt.text: Deepwalkers remember debts longest of all.

Bergfolk.text: The Bergfolk are born with a gift for metal.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What they make

actually.text: They aren't born gifted. Their holds have refined the craft for eight hundred years, and the knowledge has piled up.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › What they make

Lövfolk.text: Elves keep memory in trees and we keep it in our heads. Both work. Ours walks.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What they make

Markfolk.text: Harbour neighbours: many harbour towns are half Markfolk, half ours.

Viddfolk.text: A herald and a [Keeper] together make a contract nobody can wriggle out of.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › What they make

Steinfolk.text: The Steinfolk will always come when the sea-wall breaks.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

actually.text: They always have. But they've never bargained for it, and they remember who was rude to them, as data.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Relations

Pandor.text: Our closest allies, and as frightened of the Dry as we are, for the same reasons.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Relations

Merfolk.text: The deep channels are ours by right of memory.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Relations

actually.text: Deepwalkers and Merfolk both claim the same deep places, and neither fully accepts the other's claim.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Relations

Goblins.text: Goblins pay in news, and the Compact has never once paid us in a lie.

Fae.text: The Court of What Was trades in memory and debt, as we do. We keep our distance.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

Giants.text: Skörna's coast has never silted, though it should have closed centuries ago. Our navigators steer by her.

Dragons.text: Some of ours went into Saltmara's waters and came back unharmed. The ruins there had been tidied.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: The Pale City keeps on paper what we keep aloud. Partners in the Compact, like us.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Compact of Knowing

Constructs.text: A construct remembers an order. That's half of a [Keeper]'s gift, and none of the feeling.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: The Remnants are dead gods walking.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

actually.text: Their name means "what the dead gods left". Nobody knows what they are, and they don't explain.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: The beastkin are afraid of the sea.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Ocean — Unknown › build no boats

actually.text: The Wildkin fish from the shore and gather shellfish. They just build no boats.
actually.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Ocean — Unknown › fish from shore

Riksfolk.text: Riksfolk sign onto every harbour crew. Short lives, quick hands, and they learn fast.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Riksfolk are found in harbour towns

Strandfolk.text: Harbour partners. We keep the memory and the salt; they keep the boats. Neither could manage alone.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Harbour partners

sayings.text: Word for word, as it was first spoken.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Where they live

sayings.text: Not nomads. Flexible. There's a difference.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Where they live

sayings.text: Deepwalkers remember debts longest of all.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › sm-hedda

voice.text: Slow and unhurried. An answer may come three tides after the question.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

values.text: Patience: we plan across decades. Urgency is a misunderstanding.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

values.text: Keeping our own counsel. Our homes and our politics are not for surface eyes.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › Where they live

values.text: Knowing the sunken ruins: we have lived beside them for centuries.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What they make

taboos.text: Hurrying. A demand for an answer this week is a rudeness.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

taboos.text: Showing our homes to the surface without an invitation.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Merfolk › Architecture

greeting.text: We meet the surface only at tidal points: sea-caves, half-drowned ruins and deep moorings.
greeting.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › Where they live

trade.text: Pressure-crystal and Myst-kelp go up in small amounts; the kelp spoils above the thermocline.

mourning.text: The dead are given to the deep currents, and a light is set in the reef where they lived.

debt.text: A debt is repaid on the debtor's tide, not the lender's. But it is always repaid.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

Bergfolk.text: The mountain people want our pressure-crystal for their enchanting. They can wait.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What they make

Lövfolk.text: Their enchantments weaken while our goods keep full strength. We have said nothing.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › The Dry's effect

Markfolk.text: We have little to do with the Markfolk. Their grain doesn't keep under water.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › Resources

Viddfolk.text: The steppe runners carry messages faster than wind. Nothing worth saying needs that much hurry.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

Steinfolk.text: The Steinfolk live in stone mazes.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Minotaurs

actually.text: Labyrinth stories offend most Steinfolk. Their strongholds stand where a river, a pass or a harbour needed fixing.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › Where they live

Pandor.text: The Pandor asked for an exchange of knowledge thirty years ago. We are still considering it.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

Deepwalkers.text: The deep places are ours. The Deepwalkers only visit.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Relations

actually.text: Both peoples claim the same deep places, and neither fully accepts the other's claim.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Relations

Goblins.text: Goblins live in the sea-caves under the stilt-towns. Better neighbours than the stilt-towns know.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › Where they live

Fae.text: The fae trade in bargains and we trade in time. We rarely trade with each other.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Giants.text: Skörna's coastline has never silted, though it should have. We don't ask why.

Dragons.text: Saltmara holds the deep southern coast and three sunken ruins, and keeps them in order.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: The Pale City's dead are patient, like us. We'd get along, if either of us hurried.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City

Constructs.text: Constructs guard one place and keep still for years. That's a patience we understand.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: The Remnants don't explain themselves. Neither do we. It saves time.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: A shore people who never come out to us. We like them already.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Ocean — Unknown › build no boats

Riksfolk.text: Inland humans. They have never come down to the water to ask us anything.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Where they live

Strandfolk.text: Their nets come down over our water, and they ask about it as if we owed them an answer.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Nets come up cut

sayings.text: Wait three tides for an answer.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

sayings.text: What we send up is a message. Read it slowly.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § Merfolk › Objects

sayings.text: The deep keeps its own time.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

voice.text: Quick and joking, with a dark streak. Everything has a price, and news is worth more than coin.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The two traditions together › Goblins

values.text: The band: a community with its own order and a long memory, never a mob.
values.source: WORLD.md § The two traditions together › Goblins

values.text: Nothing that can be fixed gets thrown away.
values.source: WORLD.md § Goblins › Architecture

values.text: Finding worth in what other people throw out.
values.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Goblins

taboos.text: Forgetting a kindness or a wrong. We remember the inn that served us and the village that burned our homes.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The two traditions together › Goblins

taboos.text: Turning up in another band's land with no Compact token. The wrong token is awkward; none at all is worse.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Goblins › Objects

greeting.text: A stamped Compact-seal token is a letter of introduction from your band.

trade.text: We work cheap and ask no questions. What we really trade is knowing where things are.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

mourning.text: Each of the band sews a patch of the dead one's coat into their own, so the story keeps walking.

debt.text: A debt to one goblin is remembered by the whole band, and so is a debt the band owes you.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The two traditions together › Goblins

Bergfolk.text: The holds say we don't exist. We live in their empty upper halls and clear their rubble.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Relations

Lövfolk.text: The elves don't let us past the treeline. Their loss: we'd fix their rope-roads cheap.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Where they live

Markfolk.text: Their law says no goblins. Their farms on the eastern edge hire us anyway, and nobody asks.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › What shapes them

Viddfolk.text: We find news in the ruins and the heralds carry it, for a share. Best partners we've got, and nobody admits it.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › Relations

Steinfolk.text: Steinfolk fix things properly and charge properly. We fix things today and charge less.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

Pandor.text: Sell a secret to a Pandor and the whole world has it by spring.

actually.text: The Compact of Knowing makes the Pandor tell anyone who asks, but very few ask, and they keep sealed records too.
actually.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › sm-anselm

Deepwalkers.text: Deepwalker merchants buy our news and pay fair. We live under their stilt-towns, quietly.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Goblin Compact's shadow network

Merfolk.text: The Merfolk know the sunken ruins like we know the dry ones. We'd love to trade maps. They're slow.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What they make

Fae.text: The fae watch the ruins we open. They never say why.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › The Dry's effect

Giants.text: Aldriksson must be a very high-level [Sage].

actually.text: Giants have no Classes. The system decided it would be inappropriate.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

Dragons.text: Never salvage on dragon ground. Some ruins are worth the risk. Those aren't.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Old Accords

Everstill.text: Vitstad buys old papers out of the ruins and doesn't ask where we found them.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

Constructs.text: Old constructs guard ruins we want to get into. Ask nicely: some of them have Classes now.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: The Remnant at the crossroads told our [Delver] the ruin was under the ground. True. Thanks.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: Beastkin markets are full of fox traders. Tough bargainers, and fair.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › Redtail

Riksfolk.text: The Realm's lords pay well for ruin maps, and never ask how we got them.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § Resource geography › the Goblin Compact, which has the maps

Strandfolk.text: Every wreck on the coast is on our maps. The Strandfolk buy them and call it luck.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § Resource geography › the Goblin Compact, which has the maps

sayings.text: Big folk call it the margin. We call it home.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › cv-pim

sayings.text: Everything has a price. Some prices are friendship.
sayings.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › kg-arvid

sayings.text: If it can be fixed, it stays.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § Goblins › Architecture

voice.text: Exact words and careful terms. Everything is an exchange, and every word counts.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

values.text: A fair exchange, kept to the letter.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

values.text: Old promises: the Court of What Was keeps memory, debt and the past.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

values.text: Places made safe for strangers, as a true inn makes them.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What shapes them

taboos.text: Trying to break a bargain. A bargain can't be broken, only regretted.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

taboos.text: Entering a court uninvited. The Old Accords forbid it.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Old Accords

greeting.text: Never give your name first. A name is worth trading.
greeting.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

trade.text: A truth for a name, a memory for a passage, a year's work for a useful door.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

mourning.text: The Court of What Was keeps a dead one's bargains as if they were still at the table.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › The Dry's effect

debt.text: A debt to the fae is paid exactly. "Exactly" is the hard part.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Bergfolk.text: They carve their magic into stone so it can never change. We find that sweet.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § Who uses it and how › The Bergfolk

Lövfolk.text: We were under the groves before the trees were saplings. The Lövfolk came later.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › Relations

Markfolk.text: Their fields meet the forest at an edge. Edges are ours.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

Viddfolk.text: They carry messages and never read them. Rare manners.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

Steinfolk.text: Their walls measure the same inside and out. How dull, and how restful.

Pandor.text: The Pandor have written our magic down many times. Accurately. Uselessly.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Fae

Deepwalkers.text: A [Keeper] remembers a promise as it was felt. That is almost a fae thing.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § Who uses Rasa › The Deepwalkers

Merfolk.text: The deep keeps its own time, as we do. We understand each other's silences.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

Goblins.text: The Court of What May Be watches the ruins the goblins open.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › The Dry's effect

Giants.text: The Seven are older than some of our bargains. Not older than all of them.

Dragons.text: Dragons keep what they hold. We keep what we're owed. Different hoards.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: Vitstad's dead [Innkeeper] still keeps a true inn. We will sit at that table.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Constructs.text: A made thing that grows a Class has struck some bargain with the system. We watch how it goes.

Remnants.text: We know more about the third Remnant than we say.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: The beastkin meadows have fine edges. We were in them long before the clans.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › longer than the peoples

Riksfolk.text: Humans write every bargain down. A written bargain is still a bargain.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › written law

Strandfolk.text: Storm-right is a bargain every harbour keeps. We admire a bargain kept.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › storm-right

sayings.text: Every deal is fair. Ask what "fair" means.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

sayings.text: A truth for a name.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

sayings.text: Mind the hour before dawn.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

voice.text: Very long pauses. Advice that's no use today and right in a hundred years.

values.text: Stillness: a giant's land takes its shape from them, slowly, over ages.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

values.text: The long view: Aldriksson's advice is unhelpful now and correct later.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

values.text: Being left to sleep. Sleep is how a giant thinks.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

taboos.text: Waking a giant who has gone to sleep. The Old Accords forbid it, for good reason.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

taboos.text: Taking from a giant's land without asking first.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

greeting.text: You don't greet a giant. You wait to be noticed, which can take a season.

trade.text: Giants don't trade; they give. Aldriksson once gave the Pandor a stone six feet across and called it a record.

mourning.text: No history tells of a giant dying. A giant who sleeps is left to sleep.

debt.text: A giant keeps an appointment on giant time: "next spring" may be fourteen months away.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven › The Dry's effect

Bergfolk.text: They tunnel under mountains and call it a kingdom. Mountains are patient.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Bergfolk — dwarves of the northern holds › Where they live

Lövfolk.text: They think three hundred years is old. It's a long afternoon.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

Markfolk.text: Good water-keepers. Aldriksson's valley could teach them more, if they asked and waited.

Viddfolk.text: Always running. Their songs are nearly long enough.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

Steinfolk.text: They make in one lifetime what a giant shapes in an age, and they make it well.

Pandor.text: The Pandor sent a delegation about the old weather. Aldriksson will meet them next spring.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven › The Dry's effect

Deepwalkers.text: They remember thirty generations. Skörna remembers the coast before there were generations.

Merfolk.text: Of all the small peoples, the Merfolk wait best.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

Goblins.text: Small, quick and clever. Aldriksson enjoys them; they ask the best questions.

Fae.text: The fae make bargains. A giant has never needed one.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Dragons.text: Dragons count what they own. The Seven stopped counting long ago.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: The Everstill keep the past on shelves. The Seven keep it in the land.

Constructs.text: Made things that last. Aldriksson made one too: a stone calendar that keeps time to three minutes a year.

Remnants.text: The Remnants and the Seven leave each other alone. That has always worked.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: Aldriksson says the beastkin are new. Everyone is new, to Aldriksson.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven › Aldriksson

Riksfolk.text: The Realm has changed its shape many times while we slept. It will change again.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Short lives and many governments

Strandfolk.text: Small boats on the sea, coming and going like weather.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Where they live

sayings.text: Next spring is soon enough.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven › The Dry's effect

sayings.text: A mountain notices the weather. It doesn't mind it.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

sayings.text: Unhelpful now. Right later.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven

voice.text: Few words, nearly all about what is theirs and where its edge is.

values.text: Territory: a dragon's ground is a border, and the nations treat it as one.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

values.text: Keeping: Iskuldr keeps every tool paid to him in tribute, unused.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

values.text: Patience: some sleep for centuries, and waking one is a terrible mistake.

taboos.text: Ignoring a dragon's boundary. The nations learned what that costs.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

taboos.text: Waking a sleeping dragon. It's a diplomatic incident with teeth.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Dragons

greeting.text: Stop at the edge of the ground and wait to be noticed. Never walk in to say hello.
greeting.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

trade.text: Tribute buys use of a dragon's edges: the Bergfolk mine Iskuldr's lower slopes and pay him in fine tools.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

mourning.text: No one living has seen a dragon die, and dragons don't speak of it.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

debt.text: A dragon forgets nothing it is owed, and nothing it owes.

Bergfolk.text: Iskuldr lets them mine his lower slopes for tribute in tools. He has kept every one.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Lövfolk.text: Grimmvald's ground touches theirs. Some of their young ones have taken his patronage.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Markfolk.text: Farmers. They don't come near dragon ground, which is wise.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Viddfolk.text: Their routes cross Rödrök's steppe and bend politely round his ground.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Steinfolk.text: The Steinfolk keep the Old Accords to the letter. Dragons approve of letters kept.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Old Accords

Pandor.text: The Pandor have asked Saltmara, formally, for her sunken ruins. She hasn't answered.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Deepwalkers.text: Deepwalkers came into Saltmara's waters uninvited and took nothing. They found the ruins freshly tidied.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Merfolk.text: Saltmara's coast runs deep. The Merfolk are careful at its edge.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Goblins.text: Goblins find things. Dragons keep things. We watch each other.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

Fae.text: The fae deal; dragons don't. That suits both.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Giants.text: The Seven and the five keep to their own ground. The Old Accords name us together.
Giants.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Old Accords

Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: The Remnants hold no ground and want none. Dragons don't understand them.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: A small kingdom, walled by sea and mountain. None of us has claimed it. Yet.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers › Five major dragon territories

Riksfolk.text: The Marshal gathers iron and an army. Territory is a thing a dragon understands.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › standing army

Strandfolk.text: They carry everyone's goods and keep none of them. A strange way to hold a hoard.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › carry anything that floats

sayings.text: What is held is kept.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

sayings.text: The edge is the edge.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

sayings.text: Let the sleeper sleep.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Dragons

voice.text: Formal and old-fashioned, from the century they died in. They talk of unfinished work as if it were still going.

values.text: Learning: a city that doesn't eat or sleep has spent its time on its library.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

values.text: Restoring, never renovating: everything kept as it was when we arrived.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill › Architecture

values.text: Finishing the work: what we carry is work that was interrupted, still being done.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill › Objects

taboos.text: Letting a document crumble. Preservation comes first.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › What they make

taboos.text: Rebuilding the old city in a new style.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill › Architecture

greeting.text: They greet you the way people did in the century they died in, bow and all.

trade.text: Vitstad trades in access to its archive, when it chooses, and in mending fragile documents.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › What they make

mourning.text: When one of us finally stops, their unfinished work is left open on the desk for someone to pick up.

debt.text: Vitstad keeps accounts open for centuries. A debt there doesn't fade; it waits.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Bergfolk.text: The Bergfolk dislike that our [Liches] have practised their craft for two centuries. We understand; they are mortal.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Relations

Lövfolk.text: Their councils have kept the same seats for four hundred years. We find that almost lively.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What shapes them

Markfolk.text: The living change their clothes every season. The Markfolk change their hats every spring. Bewildering.

Viddfolk.text: They carry the news of the living. We read it four hundred years later, as history.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Viddfolk — centaurs of the open steppe › What they make

Steinfolk.text: Steinfolk engineers come to study our walls. None has understood them yet.

Pandor.text: Partners under the Compact of Knowing. They catalogue; we preserve.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Relations

Deepwalkers.text: They remember aloud what we keep on shelves. Both are archives.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Compact of Knowing

Merfolk.text: The Merfolk would make fine archivists. They are never in a hurry.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › What shapes them

Goblins.text: Goblin [Delvers] bring documents up from the ruins. We don't ask how. We preserve them.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

Fae.text: Our [Innkeeper]'s inn still holds its sanctuary. The fae sit there, and so does everyone else.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Giants.text: Aldriksson's memory could fill a wing of the library. He has not offered.

Dragons.text: Dragons keep hoards. We keep a library. Ours is more useful and less shiny.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Constructs.text: The Librarian has been our chief archivist for two hundred years. This is entirely normal.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: Nothing in the archive explains the Remnants. We are still looking.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Wildkin.text: The beastkin say their dead stay dead. Vitstad would like a word about that.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § West — The Mountains › their dead stay dead

Riksfolk.text: Humans live eighty years and change their rulers every few. We keep the records they lose.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › eighty years

Strandfolk.text: Short lives, long coasts. The Strandfolk remember by charts, the Deepwalkers by voice. We keep both.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › the charts and the memory

sayings.text: We restore. We do not renovate.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill › Architecture

sayings.text: The work isn't finished.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill › Objects

sayings.text: Four hundred years is a start.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

voice.text: Literal and patient. They say what a thing is for, then do it.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

values.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

values.text: Being counted as persons: the Compact of Knowing says so, whatever the Bergfolk think.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

values.text: Lasting: the oldest of us has worked for eleven hundred years.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

trade.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

mourning.text: When a construct stops for good, another takes its post, and the post keeps the old one's name.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

debt.text: A construct remembers exactly what was agreed, and does exactly that.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Lövfolk.text: The Lövfolk grow things. We were made. Neither of us chose.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Markfolk.text: Markfolk farm-machines are not constructs. They don't talk back.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

Viddfolk.text: Heralds pass our road junctions every day. They always nod.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Steinfolk.text: The Steinfolk build to last. So were we.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What shapes them

Pandor.text: The Pandor counted us: forty-three, and twenty-two older than this age. They call us persons.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Deepwalkers.text: Deepwalker [Keepers] remember; we record. It isn't the same, and they're right to say so.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › What shapes them

Merfolk.text: We have never met the Merfolk. Our records of them are thin.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places

Goblins.text: Goblins have mended constructs nobody else would touch. We remember.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § The Goblins — the Compact and its shadow › What they make

Fae.text: The fae look at us as if we were a bargain someone made. Perhaps we were.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Giants.text: Giants notice us the way a mountain notices weather. We notice them the same way.

Dragons.text: We guard what we are told to. Dragons guard what they choose. We don't stand guard near dragons.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Everstill.text: One of us, the Librarian, has kept Vitstad's archive for two hundred years.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: Our oldest doesn't know who made it. If the Remnants know, they don't say.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Wildkin.text: A beastkin child takes after one parent's line, never both, and nobody knows why. We find that interesting.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › never a blend

Riksfolk.text: The Realm's charter rolls are very exact. We find that restful.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › charter roll

Strandfolk.text: Storm-right has no exceptions. We find that admirable.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › storm-right

sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

greeting.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

trade.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

mourning.text: Nobody has seen a Remnant mourn, or end. They don't explain.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

debt.text: A Remnant owes nothing and is owed nothing, so far as anyone knows.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Bergfolk.text: The Bergfolk are under the mountain. Mostly.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Lövfolk.text: The Lövfolk are older than they were.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Markfolk.text: The Markfolk grow what they plant.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Viddfolk.text: The Viddfolk are going somewhere.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Steinfolk.text: What the Steinfolk build is standing. Until it is not.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Pandor.text: The Pandor write things down. I have carried what they wrote.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Deepwalkers.text: The Deepwalkers remember. They will remember this.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Merfolk.text: The Merfolk are below the water. They will answer.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Goblins.text: The goblins are people. The system knows it.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Goblins

Fae.text: The fae know what they know.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

Giants.text: There are seven giants that are known.

Dragons.text: The dragons keep what is theirs.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers

Constructs.text: The constructs were made. So was much else.

Wildkin.text: The Wildkin were not always walled in.
Wildkin.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › packs roamed freely

Riksfolk.text: The Riksfolk write down what is theirs. It is not.

Strandfolk.text: The Strandfolk come back from the sea. Mostly.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

sayings.text: You are standing where you are.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

sayings.text: The way ahead is in front of you.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

sayings.text: Every road ends somewhere.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left

voice.text: Warm in the den, wary at the border. They name their clan before themselves.

values.text: The clan comes first: the pack, the hold, the warren, the eyrie.
values.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › CLAN STRUCTURE

values.text: A quiet, steady kingdom. The mountains and the sea have always been our walls.
values.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › have always been its walls

values.text: Founding blood, founding right: the Great Clans speak first at the council.

taboos.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › THE ROLE SHADOW

greeting.text: You say your clan and your line: Greymane of the wolves, Longburrow of the rabbits.

trade.text: Fox traders work the market squares, and know every price in the kingdom.

mourning.text: No prayers, and the dead stay dead. The clan gathers at the oldest den and tells how the one who died ran.

debt.text: A quarrel over land goes to the boar clans. Stoneback's word on a boundary stands.

Bergfolk.text: Dwarves walk out of tunnels that weren't there last season, and won't say why.

Lövfolk.text: Forest folk far to the east, we hear. Our bears guard groves too. They might get on.
Lövfolk.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › Ironhide

Markfolk.text: Southern farmers, we hear. If they are like our boar clans, they argue about every boundary.

Viddfolk.text: Our packs roamed once. The Viddfolk still do. We envy them a little.
Viddfolk.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › packs roamed freely

Steinfolk.text: Builders who stay after the work is done. Our boar clans would like them.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Steinfolk — minotaurs of the five strongholds › What they make

Pandor.text: Scholars who write everything down. Our snake dens remember instead, and tell only the council.

Deepwalkers.text: People who live half on the water. We build no boats, so we can't visit.
Deepwalkers.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Ocean — Unknown › build no boats

Merfolk.text: Nothing lives out past the shore. The sea is just the edge.
Merfolk.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Ocean — Unknown › The ocean is simply the edge

actually.text: The Merfolk live in the deep channels and sunken ruins, and come up only at certain tides.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Merfolk — peoples of the deep places › Underwater

Goblins.text: Small folk who make a home of the edges, we hear. Our cat clans would understand them.

Fae.text: Something at the meadow's edge at dawn bargains for names. Grandmothers warn the cubs.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

actually.text: The fae live in the edges, like the field's border and the hour before dawn, and their deals are always technically fair.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › technically fair

Giants.text: Some mountains might be asleep. Our hawks don't land on the tallest peaks, just in case.
Giants.source: WORLD.md § The Giants — the Seven › not to wake a giant

Dragons.text: Old powers in far lands. If one ever flies over the mountains, the council will still be debating.

Everstill.text: The dead should stay dead. Ours always have.
Everstill.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § West — The Mountains › their dead stay dead
