Everstill.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § West — The Mountains › The Undead

actually.text: The undead in the passes come from deeper in the mountains, and nobody knows why. Vitstad's Everstill aren't corruption's work.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › without the involvement

Constructs.text: Made things that think? We have no word for them yet.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade › Guardians

Remnants.text: Our snake dens bring old knowledge to the council. They may know what a Remnant is. They haven't said.

Riksfolk.text: The fence-folk came from the east one fence at a time. Our packs ran those meadows once; now we only remember them.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › What the Wildkin remember

Riksfolk.text: Iron hinges, latched doors, market squares: they came west with the fence-folk. The old wolves still grumble.
Riksfolk.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › Human influence crept in

Riksfolk.text: The fence-folk came west to drive us into the sea.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › What the Wildkin remember

actually.text: They came for farmland, one charter at a time. The Realm always had easier directions to grow, and most March farmers never wanted a war.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › How the March grew

Riksfolk.text: A Riksfolk signs a treaty with one hand and moves a fence with the other.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › The Alder War and the Stone Line

actually.text: Not one stone of the Stone Line has moved in a hundred and forty years. The new trouble is harsher talk and border incidents, on both sides.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › The border now

Riksfolk.text: The fence-folk don't care for the land. They just dig it up.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › How the March grew

actually.text: A March farmer's charter roll holds every ditch and boundary back to the first fence their family dug.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › charter roll

Riksfolk.text: Their realm has had three kinds of rulers in five hundred years. Longburrow's young ones like the old republic far too much, the old bears say.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › The Clan Question, seen from the March

Strandfolk.text: Boat people far down the coast? A fox trader's story. Nobody goes out on the sea.
Strandfolk.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Ocean — Unknown › build no boats

actually.text: The Strandfolk sail the coasts east of the delta. They've never had a reason to sail the Wildkin's sea.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › nobody in the Hamnlag has had a reason

sayings.text: The mountains and the sea have always been our walls.
sayings.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › have always been its walls

sayings.text: We were here before you counted.
sayings.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › We were here before you counted

sayings.text: The oldest houses look like dens. The newest have iron hinges.
sayings.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › iron hinges

sayings.text: Old blood, old rules.
sayings.source: macro-world/race-affinities.json › old blood, old rules

voice.text: Quick and plain, with a clerk's ear. They quote the charter, then the clause, then the witnesses.
voice.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › written law

values.text: Kings come and go; the written law stays. Nobody argues with a charter.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Kings come and go

values.text: A field fenced, farmed and written down is yours, and your children's after you.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › whoever will fence it and farm it

values.text: Make your own place. A younger child doesn't wait for land; they go and find it.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › younger children, landless

taboos.text: Moving a boundary at night. A fence moves in daylight, with neighbours watching, or not at all.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › Fences in daylight

taboos.text: Leaving an insult unanswered. A March family's standing is what it's seen to do.
taboos.source: AXES.md § Notes on individual scores › visible deeds

greeting.text: You give your name and where your charter lies: Anna, of the third ditch at Alåbro.
greeting.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › Alåbro

trade.text: Any sale bigger than a cow goes in the market roll, with two witnesses. The Landslag says so.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › written law

mourning.text: No prayers. The dead one's name is read from the charter roll at the field's edge, and the heir's is written in.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › charter roll

debt.text: A debt goes before the [Reeve], who writes it down. Once it's written, the whole village holds you to it.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › [Reeve]

Bergfolk.text: We buy their iron. The Marshal's army has bought a great deal of it lately, and the holds are asking why.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › started asking what it's for

Lövfolk.text: An elf remembers when the Realm was a republic. Ask one how it ended, and clear your evening.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › a single Lövfolk

Lövfolk.text: The elves think they're better than everyone.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Elves

actually.text: Lövfolk opinions set hard after three hundred years; their councils have held the same seats for four centuries. Their young often leave.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What shapes them

Markfolk.text: Orc farmers across the fens. We buy their grain in bad years, and hate needing to.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Relations

Markfolk.text: Orcs are warriors first. Give one a field and he'll want a fight over it.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Orcs

actually.text: The Markfolk are the continent's best farmers. A Level 35 [Watermaster] is more powerful than many a [Knight].
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Markfolk — orcs of the southern plains › more powerful than many a [Knight]

Viddfolk.text: The Marshal's letters go by herald, and every word is remembered. She knows it.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Relations

Steinfolk.text: The Steinfolk build in stone, not magic. Whatever the Dry does, their walls will stand.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Dry's political effect › who build in stone

Pandor.text: The pandas have a record of everything, even the years the Realm would rather forget.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Dry's political effect › The Pandor have the records

Deepwalkers.text: A contract a Deepwalker keeper witnessed binds in every court of the Realm.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › considered legally binding

Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Merfolk

actually.text: The Merfolk are real. Strandfolk nets over Merfolk waters come up cut.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Nets come up cut

Goblins.text: Goblins know every ruin and sell the maps. The March lords pay, and don't ask how.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § Resource geography › the Goblin Compact, which has the maps

Fae.text: A fae deal is a trick. Never make one at the edge of a wood.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

actually.text: Fae deals are always technically fair. The trouble is what "fair" means to someone a thousand years old.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Giants.text: The Seven are older than any crown. The Old Accords say leave them be, and even the Marshal does.
Giants.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › no warfare in Giant or Dragon

Dragons.text: Dragons are wicked, and hoard gold to spite us.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Dragons

actually.text: Dragons aren't evil. Their goals just don't fit our ideas of right and wrong.
actually.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Dragons

Everstill.text: The Pale City's dead are the corruption's work.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

actually.text: The Everstill died and didn't stay dead without any help from the corruption: their Classes carried on.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Constructs.text: Constructs guard the road junctions and ruins that nobody else wants to.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: Ask the thing at the Threefold Crossroads a question and you'll get a true answer. Not a useful one.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left › Threefold Crossroads

Wildkin.text: The West March was fenced by charter, in daylight, with witnesses. By our law every field of it is fair.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › Fences in daylight

Wildkin.text: The western meadows were empty when our people came. Nobody lived on land with no fence.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › Why they believed it was right

actually.text: Wildkin packs roamed and hunted those meadows for generations. Their dens moved with the game, so the land was used, just never fenced.
actually.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Beastkin Kingdom (primary setting) › packs roamed freely

Wildkin.text: The old ruins over the Alå were built by our ancestors. We were there first.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › Why they believed it was right

actually.text: The ruins are older than the beastkin kingdom and look built by human hands, but nobody knows who built them. Nothing ties them to the Realm.
actually.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § Below — The Underworld › Human ruins

Wildkin.text: The Highfang wants the March back, and is only waiting for a weak year.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › The border now

actually.text: The Wildkin have never been conquerors. Their council is debating, not plotting, and the corruption is pushing both sides.
actually.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § East — The Human Lands › The beastkin are not conquerors

Wildkin.text: The Stone Line has held for a hundred and forty years. The boar clans set the stones with us, and their word on a boundary is good.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › The Alder War and the Stone Line

Wildkin.text: Four seats on their council and none for the rabbits. And they call us unsettled.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › The Clan Question, seen from the March

Strandfolk.text: Kin by blood, strangers by law. They pay no due to any crown, and the Marshal would like a harbour.
Strandfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Relations

sayings.text: Kings come and go. The Landslag stays.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Riksfolk — humans of the Realm › Kings come and go

sayings.text: A fence moves in daylight, or not at all.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › Fences in daylight

sayings.text: Dig the ditch, build the fence, write it down.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › They dug a ditch

sayings.text: Four seats and none for the rabbits, and they call us unsettled.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The West March and the Wildkin border › The Clan Question, seen from the March

voice.text: Loud across water, short on deck. Every order said once, plainly, because a misheard one drowns people.
voice.source: AXES.md § Notes on individual scores › Strandfolk

values.text: Storm-right: in a storm every harbour is open to every boat, whatever its flag or its debts.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › storm-right

values.text: The boat next to yours will come when you call. Be that boat.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › will come when they call

values.text: Nobody rules a harbour town but its own shipmasters.
values.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › its own council of shipmasters

taboos.text: Turning a boat away in a storm. A harbour that did would lose its place in the Hamnlag.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › that broke storm-right would lose its place in the Hamnlag

taboos.text: Staying put because someone told you to.
taboos.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › patience with anyone who wants them to stay put

greeting.text: You call out your boat's name first, then your own, then your harbour.
greeting.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Hamnlag

trade.text: Freight is paid by weight, on scales every Hamnlag harbour keeps the same.
trade.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › a set of weights and measures

mourning.text: No prayers. A drowned sailor's name is cut into the harbour wall, and every boat in port sounds its horn once.
mourning.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › The sea, and the short lives

debt.text: A Hamnlag debt is witnessed by a Deepwalker keeper. Nobody argues with one.
debt.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › witnessed by a Deepwalker

Bergfolk.text: Bergfolk iron for our nails and anchors, and they price it like gold.
Bergfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Scarce: farmland, metal

Lövfolk.text: The elves think they're better than everyone.
Lövfolk.source: WORLD.md § Safe to use freely › Elves

actually.text: Lövfolk opinions set hard after three hundred years; their councils have held the same seats for four centuries. Their young often leave.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Lövfolk — elves of the eastern canopy › What shapes them

Markfolk.text: Our best customer. Delta grain goes to half the continent in our holds.
Markfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Half the delta's grain

Viddfolk.text: Hamnlag letters go inland by herald. Anyone who travels for a living is all right by us.
Viddfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › respect anyone who travels for a living

Steinfolk.text: A harbour wall should be Steinfolk stone. We'd hire them for every one, if we could afford it.
Steinfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Scarce: farmland, metal, stone

Pandor.text: Tell a Deepwalker keeper something and the pandas will hear of it. They share one law.
Pandor.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › Compact of Knowing

Deepwalkers.text: Harbour partners: they keep the salt, the charts and the memory; we build the boats and fill them.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › keep the salt, the charts and the memory

Deepwalkers.text: A keeper never misremembers. That's why their word is good.
Deepwalkers.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › witnessed by a Deepwalker

actually.text: The Dry touches a keeper's memory first. Some have begun to misremember, and they fear it more than anything.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Deepwalkers — coastal peoples of the long memory › They begin to misremember

Merfolk.text: The Merfolk cut our nets on purpose, to drive us off their water.
Merfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Nets come up cut

actually.text: Nobody can prove who cuts the nets. The Merfolk don't answer when asked.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Nobody can prove why

Goblins.text: Every wreck on the coast is on a goblin map. Buy one, and don't ask how they know.
Goblins.source: WORLD.md § Resource geography › the Goblin Compact, which has the maps

Fae.text: A fae deal is a trick. Never make one on a calm sea at dusk.
Fae.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › Where they live

actually.text: Fae deals are always technically fair. The trouble is what "fair" means to someone a thousand years old.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Fae — the Hollow Courts › What they make

Giants.text: The Old Accords say no fighting in Giant or Dragon country. That goes for crews ashore too.
Giants.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › no warfare in Giant or Dragon

Dragons.text: Saltmara holds the deep southern coast. Our pilots steer well round her waters.
Dragons.source: WORLD.md § The Dragons — the territorial powers › Saltmara

Everstill.text: The Pale City's dead are the corruption's work.
Everstill.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

actually.text: The Everstill died and didn't stay dead without any help from the corruption: their Classes carried on.
actually.source: WORLD.md § The Everstill — undead of the Pale City › Where they live

Constructs.text: Constructs guard old junctions and ruins nobody else wants. Not one has ever asked us for a berth.
Constructs.source: WORLD.md § The Constructs — the Unmade and Remade

Remnants.text: A harbour story says something at the Threefold Crossroads answers any question. Truly, and uselessly.
Remnants.source: WORLD.md § The Remnants — what the dead gods left › Threefold Crossroads

Wildkin.text: Past where the coast turns west there's nothing but sea.
Wildkin.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Their charts end

actually.text: Past the Realm lies the Wildkin's coast, where beastkin fish from the shore and build no boats.
actually.source: macro-world/setting-corewarden.md § The Ocean — Unknown › build no boats

Riksfolk.text: Kin by blood, strangers by law. The Marshal wants a harbour, and she can keep wanting.
Riksfolk.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Relations

sayings.text: Every harbour is open in a storm.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › storm-right

sayings.text: Be the boat that comes when called.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › will come when they call

sayings.text: Our charts end where the coast turns west. For now.
sayings.source: WORLD.md § The Strandfolk — humans of the harbour coast › Their charts end
